title: Halfway Between Two Places: Find the Midpoint
description: Find the exact geographic midpoint with the Halfway Between Two Places calculator — half-distance in miles and km for both sides. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, the halfway point between New York and Los Angeles sits at 39.5103, −97.1601 in central Kansas — approx. 1,223 miles (1,968 km) from each city, and approx. 52 miles northeast of Salina.
quick_answer: The Halfway Between Two Places calculator finds the true geographic midpoint between any two locations, measured along the surface of the Earth rather than on a flat map. Enter two places and it shows the midpoint on a map, its coordinates, and the equal half-distance in miles and kilometres.

body.t: Two people driving toward each other should split distance, not postcodes. Find the midpoint, then look at which town sits near it — the geographic answer starts the conversation, the map finishes it.

New York to Los Angeles is approx. 2,445.6 miles (3,935.8 km) in a straight line, so the halfway point lies 1,222.8 miles (1,967.9 km) from each — at 39.5103, −97.1601 in central Kansas, approx. 52 miles (84 km) northeast of Salina. Nobody's mental map puts the middle of that trip in Kansas, which is exactly why the calculation is worth doing.

London to Paris totals approx. 213.5 miles (343.5 km); the midpoint, 106.7 miles (171.8 km) from each, falls in the English Channel at 50.1885, 1.1467 — approx. 29.4 km (18.3 mi) off Dieppe on the French coast. A wet midpoint is a normal result: the tool reports the true point, and the nearest town is your practical meeting place.

faq: Is the halfway point the same as averaging the two latitudes and longitudes?

No — and the difference matters. Averaging coordinates treats the Earth as flat graph paper; over long distances, especially east–west ones, the averaged point can sit far from the true surface midpoint. This calculator finds the midpoint along the great-circle path on the sphere.
What if the midpoint falls in the sea or somewhere unreachable?

That is a normal, honest result — the London–Paris midpoint is in the English Channel. Use the coordinates as the reference point, then choose the nearest practical town; the tool shows the surrounding map precisely so you can do that sensibly.
Does halfway mean both people drive the same time?

Not necessarily. Halfway here is equal distance. Equal time depends on each side's roads, speeds and traffic, so for a timed meeting compare both journeys with the Driving Distance Calculator or a Drive Time Map as well.
Can I find the middle of three or more places?
This calculator is built for two places. For several, the Geographic Center Finder balances many points at once and is the right tool for team meetups and facility placement.

It is the exact midpoint of the great-circle path on the mean sphere — the same model the distances use. For everyday planning that is far more precision than the decision needs; the practical limit is choosing where near the point to actually meet.
Can I use coordinates instead of town names?
Yes. Enter either place by searching, clicking the map, or supplying coordinates, which is the reliable route for rural points, trailheads and places with common names.
Why does the midpoint of an east–west trip bend toward the pole?

Because the shortest surface path between two points at the same latitude is not the latitude line — it is a great circle, which bulges toward the nearer pole. The midpoint of that path inherits the bend.
